---
title: "GM Session Guide: Chapter 5 (The Wrath of Mars)"
subtitle: "GM guide — Chapter 5"
---

*The crystal-star focus is failing. The party descends past a dead king who has been fighting since 52 BC to a granite altar where a starving god waits. No option at the end saves everyone. That is the point.*

**Level:** 7 (final, no further advancement) · **Players:** 6 (Iris, Julia Jana, Tanit, Rivia, Ursula, Brian) · **Time:** 3-4 hrs · **Type:** Final dungeon crawl + divine confrontation

---

<div class="session-tree">

<details open>
<summary>📋 Session Quick-Reference — The Whole Session in One Page</summary>

| | |
|---|---|
| **Central question** | What do you do with a weapon a god will not stop wanting back? |
| **What must happen** | (1) The party descends from Chapter 4's Core Room, through Vercingetorix's true final stand, to the Antechamber of Mars. (2) The party decides the spear's fate: destroy it, give it to Rome, or give it back to Mars. All three are real endings. |
| **Player goal** | Survive the dungeon, learn the true story from Vercingetorix's Final Death, and choose. |
| **Real stakes** | Whether anyone volunteers to become the vault's new guardian (Destroy). Whether the party delivers the sealed iron box to Rome (Give to Rome). Whether the party can live with Mars walking away vindicated (Give to Mars). |
| **Session peak moment** | Vercingetorix's Final Death: for one minute, the man behind two centuries of undeath is lucid, and answers three questions truthfully before dissolving to ash. |
| **Closing image** | The crystal-star's light drains out behind the party as they climb. By the time they reach the surface, the marsh is just a marsh again. |

**NPCs active this session:**

| NPC | Location at session start | Wants | Role this session |
|---|---|---|---|
| The contubernium (Party) | Convergence Hall approach | Decide the fate of the spear; face the war-god | Operating alone; carries Lucius's locked box |
| Vercingetorix Bound | Convergence Hall portal | Fall in a way that finally counts | Scene 3 gatekeeper -- [Vercingetorix Bound](../npcs/vercingetorix_bound.json) (CR 11, AC 18, HP 150), reveals unmaking chains |
| The Session 1 Wight-general | Branch-dependent, Antechamber only | See his three-century oath discharged | One-line cameo, only if spared in Session 1 -- see Scene 4 |
| Mars (Diminished Avatar) | Antechamber dais | Reclaim the spear, keep this last tribute-line open | Divine Antagonist -- [Mars](../npcs/mars.json) (CR 20, AC 22/16, HP 300), dynamic 3-round ritual |
| Janus (Threshold Vision) | Antechamber archway | Remind mortals that war is neither simple good nor evil | Dual-faced omen at Scene 4 entrance |

**What is NOT in this session:** Legate Corvinus and Augur Cassia remain at Fort Vindolanda (epilogue only). Centurion Varro and Tribune Lucius are fallen. The old fort-arena "divine trial" is completely retired.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 0: The Crystal Is Failing</summary>

**Read aloud:**

> *The crystal-star's light does not fade when the demon guarding it falls. It gets worse. Cracks spread across its faces like frost across a window, and each one lets out a note too low to be a sound, felt in the teeth more than heard. The floor of the Core Room is warm. Somewhere below, something that has been sleeping under all this weight is starting to notice you.*

> *In the silence where Tribune Lucius once stood, the stone floor shudders. The locked box of his personal effects is still in your pack, but the choice ahead belongs entirely to your contubernium. Whatever this crystal feeds, it just fed it more than it wanted -- and the only stairs lead down.*

The crystal cannot be destroyed at the Core Room -- Chapter 4 established this. The party descends alone toward the source.

**Checks:**
- DC 13 Intelligence (Arcana) (passive): the cracking pattern matches divine attention, not structural failure.
- DC 12 Wisdom (Survival) (active, gauging descent time): warmth increases at a readable rate -- 3-4 scenes remain before it matters mechanically.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 1: The Sunken Armory and the Choking Hall</summary>

Load `s5_mars_vault_overview.html`/`.jpg`, zones 2-4.

> *The passage narrows fast. Old weapon racks line a room that has not seen a living hand in longer than the fort has stood. Half the blades have rusted to lace. The other half are untouched, as if the room itself decided which ones still mattered. Beyond it, a hall barely three men wide, walls scored with symbols the torchlight will not sit still on.*

- DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) (active): untouched weapons carry the ram's-eye stamp -- Mars's blessing. Taking one counts as a Belatucadrus-grade consecrated weapon for this session.
- DC 12 Constitution (active, pushing through Choking Hall): failure deals 1d4 poison damage from atmospheric pressure.

**Encounter:** 2 × **[Wraith](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/17064-wraith)** (*Monster Manual* p. 302 — CR 5, AC 13, HP 67). Incorporeal shades of legionaries who perished in the vault; *Life Drain* (+6, 4d6+3 necrotic, DC 14 Con save vs max HP reduction).

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 2: The Convergence Hall — Three Passages</summary>

Load `s5_mars_vault.html`/`.jpg`, zone 3.

> *The hall opens into three throats of stone, all leading the same direction by different roads. Something about the air says only one of these was meant to be walked.*

| Passage | Contents |
|---|---|
| Left (west) | Pressure-plate rune, DC 14 Perception to spot. Trigger: 3d6 necrotic, 30-ft burst, DC 15 Dexterity half. A dead cultist's journal confirms the chieftains knew what they served. |
| Center | 6 × **[Zombie](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/17069-zombie)** (*Monster Manual* p. 316 — CR 1/4, AC 8, HP 22, *Undead Fortitude* DC 5 + damage taken to survive at 1 HP). Fast clearing for martial cleaves or Turn Undead. |
| Right (east) | 1 × **[Wight](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/17054-wight)** (*Monster Manual* p. 300 — CR 3, AC 14, HP 45) + 2 × **[Specter](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/17017-specter)** (*Monster Manual* p. 289 — CR 1, AC 12, HP 22). Ranged longsword and life drain ambush. |

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 3: Vercingetorix's Last Stand</summary>

> *He stands where the three passages become one, and for the first time since the fort's gate, you see him clearly. The wounds from that night never closed. They never will. His armor is Gallic work two centuries out of fashion, rusted through in places where a living man would already be dead of infection ten times over. He is not breathing. He was never going to stop being here.*

> *"Again," he says, in Latin thick with an accent that predates the Empire itself. "Always again. Tell me this time is the one that ends it."*

**[Vercingetorix Bound](../npcs/vercingetorix_bound.json)** (*CR 11 Undead*, AC 18, HP 150):
- **Parry (Reaction):** +4 AC against one melee attack.
- **Sword of the Last Charge:** +8 to hit, 2d6+5 slashing + 2d8 necrotic.
- **Relentless (1/day):** When reduced to 0 HP, drops to 1 HP instead and roars *"FINISH IT!"* unless hit by radiant/Belatucadrus damage.
- **Champion's Duel:** If Ursula or Brian steps forward, he accepts a 1-on-1 clash with honor.

**Final Death:** 1 minute of lucidity. Delivers the tactical key to Mars's defeat:
*"The granite altar... four massive iron chain winches in the floor... Caesar's siege engineers forged them from Gallic steel to bind a god's avatar. Lock the four iron rings... they will drag Mars down and shatter his divine invulnerability. Only then can the spear be broken on the anvil!"*

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 4: The Antechamber of Mars & Threshold of Janus</summary>

Load `s5_mars_confrontation.html`/`.jpg`.

**Threshold of Janus:** At the entrance archway, a dual-faced vision of Janus flickers in the red light: *"Mars is neither good nor evil. He is war itself. Choose how you cross this threshold."*

> *The passage opens into a circle wide enough to lose an army in. Twelve stones stand at its edge like an audience that arrived centuries early. At the center, a granite altar, chained to the floor by links thick as a man's arm...*

> *On the dais stands Mars: lean, scarred, starved by two centuries of peace, his bronze armor dented and black with dried gore. "MORTALS," he says. "Now choose, and choose knowing I will remember which one you make."*

**Cameo of the Wight-general:** If spared in Session 1, his spirit rises once: *"I held this three hundred years so it would not have to end like this. I am glad I do not have to decide."* Released upon decision.

**Stat block: [Mars](../npcs/mars.json)** (*Divine Avatar*, CR 20, AC 22, HP 300):
- Multiattack (4 Divine Pilum, +12 to hit, range 60 ft, 2d8+7 piercing + 2d8 radiant).
- Divine Smite (1/round, +4d8 radiant).
- War Cry (DC 18 Wis or Frightened). Legendary Resistance 3/day.
- Legendary Actions (3/round: Strike, God's Eye, Summon Fallen).

</details>

<details>
<summary>⚖️ Decision Point: The Three Horrible Options</summary>

| Option | Requires | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Destroy it completely (Dynamic Ritual)** | **Round 1:** Lock chain winches (DC 13 Athletics/Thieves' Tools) -> Mars loses Legendary Resistance, AC drops from 22 to 15!<br>**Round 2:** Sever bloodline (DC 14 Religion/Arcana) -> Mars Multiattack drops from 4 to 2, smite silenced!<br>**Round 3:** Shatter spear on anvil! | **Someone must take the chains permanently.** With Lucius dead, **a PC must step forward** to become the eternal guardian. If no volunteer, the ritual unravels. |
| **2. Give it to Rome** | Party takes custody in an iron lockbox to deliver to Corvinus/Rome. Mars deals a furious 1-round parting strike (30-40 party dmg) and departs. | Vindolanda safe today; weapon returns to Rome to drive future emperors mad. |
| **3. Give it back to Mars** | Return spear to altar. Mars departs satisfied without violence. | No one bleeds today; god walks away vindicated, free to feed again. |

</details>

<details>
<summary>🏛️ Epilogue and DM Notes</summary>

Return to Fort Vindolanda:
- **Corvinus and Cassia** greet the survivors in the principia.
- **Varro is dead:** his quarters dark; a small wine offering at the repaired north gate. Ursula faces the gate with heavy silence.
- **Lucius is dead:** his locked box holds a carved Germanic horse, amber token, and posthumous citizenship recommendations for the party.
- **Citizenship:** Corvinus and Cassia co-sign the imperial seals, securing *Civis Romanus* for the party.

</details>
